stories.topic: CHINA / CNY / LI QIANG / CENTRAL HUIJIN / EQUITIES / ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE / CAPITAL MARKETS
stories.headline: China’s cabinet plans stronger support for equities
stories.body: Reuters reported a State Council meeting chaired by Premier Li Qiang setting out plans for stronger capital-market stabilisation, a larger Central Huijin role and longer-term institutional investment. Listed companies would be encouraged to increase dividends and share buybacks. Reuters observed the technology-focused STAR 50 index up 12% during afternoon trading; the exact quotation time was unavailable, so this is a historical intraday observation rather than a closing return or executable quote. The preview does not assign a new funding amount.
stories.analysis: State-backed buying can support liquidity and sentiment without establishing stronger household demand or sustainable corporate profitability.
stories.watch_next: Actual institutional purchases, policy implementation and the breadth of earnings and cash-flow improvement.

stories.topic: INDONESIA / IDR / FISCAL POLICY / ENERGY SUBSIDIES / OIL / INFLATION / SOVEREIGN DEBT
stories.headline: Indonesia considers higher subsidised fuel prices as budget pressure increases
stories.body: Four sources told Reuters that Indonesia was considering raising subsidised fuel prices in early 2027. No final decision or increase size was established. The 2026 energy subsidy budget was expected to reach IDR500 trillion, about US$27.2 billion at the report’s conversion and 30% above the original allocation. Those are expected costs, not a final realised annual total. Existing subsidised prices were IDR10,000 per litre for 90-octane petrol and IDR6,800 for diesel. The Finance Ministry spokesperson said it had no knowledge of discussions on future subsidies.
stories.analysis: Keeping subsidies protects purchasing power while sustaining budget pressure; reducing them could ease fiscal costs while raising consumer inflation.
stories.watch_next: A formal government decision, revised budget figures and Bank Indonesia guidance.

stories.topic: CHINA / MANUFACTURING / PMI / ECONOMIC FORECASTS / EXPORTS / DOMESTIC DEMAND
stories.headline: Reuters poll forecasts another month of contraction in China’s official manufacturing PMI
stories.body: A Reuters poll of 13 economists forecast November’s official manufacturing PMI at 49.4, against October’s actual 49.3. The private RatingDog manufacturing PMI was forecast at 51.5, versus October’s actual 52. A reading below 50 signals contraction and above 50 expansion; index levels are not output-growth percentages. These are forecasts for November, not released November results. The source report’s watch dates are 30 November for the official survey and 1 December for the private survey.
stories.analysis: A stock-market rally and an expected contractionary manufacturing survey measure different conditions. Technology strength does not establish broad domestic recovery.
stories.watch_next: The actual official and private PMI releases, new orders and domestic-demand indicators.

stories.topic: CHINA / HONG KONG / CHINA SHENHUA / 1088 / COAL / EQUITIES / CORPORATE CREDIT / SHARE PLACEMENT
stories.headline: China Shenhua Energy sets discounted placement terms with proceeds intended for debt repayment
stories.body: Reuters-attributed reporting described China Shenhua Energy’s planned placement of 177 million new Hong Kong H shares at HK$38.10 each, a 7.7% discount to the preceding HK$41.28 close. The stated gross fundraising amount was about HK$6.74 billion, or US$860 million, for onshore debt repayment and working capital. These placement terms and intended uses do not establish that all funds have settled or that debt has already been repaid. The source dashboard’s completed-fundraising shorthand and later share-price observations are not treated as independently verified settlement or price outcomes in this preview.
stories.analysis: Equity funding can improve financing flexibility while diluting existing shareholders; creditor benefits depend on actual debt repayment.
stories.watch_next: Placement completion, cash received, debt repayment and subsequent leverage.

stories.topic: AUSTRALIA / LNG / NATURAL GAS / ENERGY / ASIAN IMPORTERS / REGULATION
stories.headline: Australia passes legislation reserving part of LNG production for domestic use
stories.body: Reuters-attributed reporting said Australia’s Parliament passed a gas-reservation scheme requiring LNG exporters to set aside up to 20% of production for domestic use from 2028. Western Australia is exempt from the national scheme and already has a separate 15% reservation policy. These percentages belong to different frameworks and are not additive. Passage of the legislation is distinct from the future domestic supply obligation taking effect.
stories.analysis: Domestic supply availability and Asian import arrangements could change; actual effects depend on implementation and contracts.
stories.watch_next: Implementation rules, affected LNG projects and regional supply arrangements.
